title: IVR vs AI Voice Agents: From Call Routing to Resolution
summary: Compare IVR and AI voice agents by what happens to the caller's request: understanding context, completing work, and transferring to a human with context.
body_markdown:
[Idaho Housing and Finance Association](https://www.bland.ai/customers/ihfa) was taking about 4,000 calls a day. Before anyone could help, callers spent roughly a minute in a push-button menu and another minute being verified by a person. A transfer meant being verified again. The customer hadn't changed, but the department had.


Idaho Housing replaced the menu with a Bland agent connected to its existing verification APIs. The agent authenticated callers up front and passed the verified information to employees before they picked up. Average call length fell from about seven and a half minutes to six, and the organization estimates annual savings of $750,000.


Compare IVR and AI voice agents by how much work you remove for the caller and how much you complete before an employee needs to join.


### **The difference shows up after the greeting**#


An interactive voice response system, or IVR, uses keypad input or speech to route callers and provide automated service. Modern systems can also complete transactions, including payments and appointment changes, as[Genesys' IVR overview](https://www.genesys.com/definitions/what-is-ivr) explains.


Try one request end to end. A patient needs to move a scan before a follow-up visit and can only get a ride on Thursdays. A menu can route the call to scheduling. An agent handling the scheduling work needs to keep both constraints and find a suitable slot.


Then follow the action. Did the calendar accept the change? Was the old appointment handled correctly? Did the patient receive the required confirmation? The Thursday ride and the follow-up date should survive every step.


The agent must leave decisions about whether it is medically appropriate to delay a scan to the clinical team. Its job is to find an appointment within the constraints that team has approved.


### **A transfer can finish the job or start it over**#


The[CFPB's 2025 complaint report](https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_2025-cr-annual-report_2026-03.pdf) records consumers describing “transfers to wrong departments for assistance.” Getting a call out of one queue is easy to count. It gives the next employee and the caller very little if the problem arrives without its context.


At Idaho Housing, carrying verification forward removed work that callers and employees had been doing twice. For the Thursday appointment, that means carrying the scan, follow-up deadline, available transport, and actions already attempted into the handoff.


[Bland's warm transfers](https://www.bland.ai/blog/warm-transfers) can brief the receiving employee before merging the calls. Check whether that employee can continue from the briefing without asking the customer to reconstruct the call.


### **Resolution is visible outside the conversation**#


Containment measures how many calls stayed within automation. Check the calendar, account record, or connected transfer to see what happened to the request. A transfer to the person with the right authority can be a successful result.


For scheduling, review successful and incorrect changes, repeat contacts about the same request, and whether transfers reached the right team. Ask callers about their experience and check the business record to confirm what was completed.


For a wider rollout, the[call center automation guide](https://www.bland.ai/blog/where-to-start-call-center-automation) covers pilot design; this comparison starts with one request that both systems should be able to carry through.


Run the Thursday appointment through the existing system and the proposed agent, including the handoff. At Idaho Housing, progress meant the customer stopped providing the same thing twice. Here it means they stop explaining why Thursday matters and end up with an appointment they can attend.
